BIRLA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY, MESRA, RANCHI
(MID SEMESTER EXAMINATION MO/SP20**)
CLASS: BARCH   SEMESTER : I
BRANCH: ARCHITECTURE   SESSION : MO/2022

SUBJECT: AR101 PRINCIPLES OF ARCHITECTURE
TIME: 02 HOURS   FULL MARKS: 25

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. The question paper contains 5 questions each of 5 marks and total 25 marks.
2. Attempt all questions.
3. The missing data, if any, may be assumed suitably.
4. Tables/Data handbook/Graph paper etc., if applicable, will be supplied to the candidates
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


   CO BL
Q.1(a) Discuss the design process with the help of a flowchart. [2] 1 Understand
Q.1(b) How did Vitruvius, the roman architect, define building? [3] 1 Remember


Q.2(a) Who  is  an  architect?  Under  which  Act there  are registered  as a professional
body?
[2] 1 Remember
Q.2(b) How does the  teaching  in the architecture  curriculum include the  complexity
and openness to mimic real-world problems?
[3] 2 Apply


Q.3(a) How do transformation principles help in the design process? [2] 3 Apply
Q.3(b) Analyse the difference in ordering principles: Repetition and Rhythm [3] 2 Analyse


Q.4(a) Mention at least  six  ordering  principles  that  help  the  designer  in the design
process.
[2] 2 Remember
Q.4(b) Why did the  designer  use  Dominance  as  an ordering  principle? Mention three
types which create it.
[3] 2 Evaluate


Q.5(a) What is the prime generator of shape? Mention the properties of shape. [2] 2 Remember
Q.5(b) How does a  designer use a different  form  of spatial organisation of  different
forms?
[3] 2 Understand

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Q1 (a) In what ways is the golden ratio related to Fibonacci series? [2]
Q1 (b) Who illustrated the concept of Modular? Write about Fibonacci series with equation? [3]


Q2 (a) What is Biomimicry? What kind of approach an architect took to mimic lotus flower in
Lotus temple structure?
[2]
Q2 (b) How  the  light  and  space  elements  of  biophilic  design  you can  utilize  based  on  the
quality of light?
[3]


Q3 (a) Mention the kind of transformation in following:
a) A sphere transformed to ellipsoidal form by elongating axis.
b) Physically attaching one or more subordinate form to its volume.
[2]
Q3 (b) Discuss different form of spatial organization. [3]


Q4 (a) Mention eight ordering principle to make your design complete. [2]
Q4 (b) How repetition, pattern and rhythm are different from each other? [3]


Q5 (a) What is the prime generator of form? Write down the properties of form. [2]
Q5 (b) What are the elements of design? Design a composition using three geometric figures to
create symmetry.
[3]

INSTRUCTIONS:

Q1 (a) Outline the Architect’s Contribution towards culture and the society. [2]
Q1 (b) Describe the Architectural Design & Building Process & the Architect’s role in it. [3]


Q2 (a)
Describe the structure of Architectural Education w.r.t Curricular content (i.e. subjects
taught) in - History of Architecture, Materials and Methods of Construction, and Building
Services. List the various subjects under the above-mentioned heads.
[2]
Q2 (b)
List  the  various  subjects  under  the  below-mentioned  heads  –  Structural  Subjects,
Electives and Building Science.
[3]


Q3 (a) Explain architecture in terms of the three variables Need, context and form. [2]
Q3 (b) Explain  the  basic  design  elements, point,  line  and  plane  and their  incorporation  in
architecture.
[3]


Q4 (a) Show the application of sphere and cylinder in Architecture. [2]
Q4 (b) Analyse the different Principles of Organization of Form & Space, taking architectural
examples.
[3]


Q5 (a) Apply Fractrals w.r.t to their applications giving two architectural examples. [2]
Q5 (b)
Evaluate Biophilic Architecture with respect to its merits and analyze bio-mimicry in
terms of creating healing environment.
[3]
